cadence.runoff_rule: Single-member constituencies: elected in the first round with an absolute majority of votes cast and a quarter of registered voters; otherwise candidates with 12.5 percent of registered voters (10 percent before 1976, 5 percent before 1966) go to a second round a week later, won by a plurality (art. L123 to L126). In 1986 only, list proportional representation by département. The Assembly's powers end the third Tuesday of June of the fifth year after its election (art. LO121), so after the 2024 dissolution the next regular election falls in June 2029.
cadence.vacancy_rule: Substitutes fill most vacancies (art. LO176); otherwise by-elections within three months, except in the last year of the term (art. LO178). After a dissolution (art. 12 of the Constitution) a general election is held 20 to 40 days later, as in 1962, 1968, 1981, 1988, 1997, and 2024.

Regional lists with département sections: a list with an absolute majority in the first round wins; otherwise lists with 10 percent of votes cast go to a second round a week later (lists with 5 percent may merge). The leading list takes a quarter of the seats (11 seats in Corsica, 11 in Martinique, 11 in Guyane) and the rest are shared by highest average among lists with 5 percent. The 2015 councils served until 2021, and the 2021 elections moved from March to June (loi n° 2021-191), with the next in March 2028.

For 2026, the count covers communes alone: the Interior Ministry's 34,875 in metropolitan France and the overseas departments, less the six destroyed villages near Verdun that have no voters and are run by a commission the prefect appoints, plus the 33 of New Caledonia, the 2 of Saint-Pierre-and-Miquelon, and the 48 of French Polynesia, each from the State's services there. The sector councils of Paris, Lyon, and Marseille count with their commune. Saint-Barthélemy and Saint-Martin elect territorial councils, not municipal ones, so they are left out. 1989 is the Interior Ministry's count of mayors elected after that year's renewal, one per commune.

cadence.runoff_rule: Communes of 1,000 inhabitants or more (3,500 before 2014): closed lists, elected in the first round with an absolute majority, otherwise lists with 10 percent go to a second round; the leading list takes half the seats and the rest go by highest average among lists with 5 percent. The mayor is then elected by the council.
cadence.vacancy_rule: Partial or complete by-elections within three months when a council loses a third of its members or the mayor must be replaced without a full council.

classes.name: Élections sénatoriales
classes.note: Senators are elected in each département and overseas collectivity, and by the French abroad, by an electoral college of deputies, regional and departmental councillors, and delegates of the municipal councils (about 93,000 electors for series 2 in 2026). Constituencies with three or more seats use list proportional representation (highest average); those with one or two use a two-round majority vote. Renewed by thirds every three years for nine-year terms from 1959 to 2004 (series A, B, and C); since 2011 by halves every three years for six-year terms (series 1 and 2), after a transition in 2004 and 2008. The Senate's own archive lists every renewal.

cadence.runoff_rule: Majority constituencies: absolute majority and a quarter of the college in the first or second round, plurality in the third (art. L294).

Constituencies electing one or two senators: two rounds the same day, absolute majority and a quarter of the electors in the first, plurality in the second; three or more: list proportional representation, highest average (art. L294 and L295).
cadence.vacancy_rule: Substitutes or the next on the list replace senators; otherwise a by-election within three months, except in the year before a renewal.

classes.note: Universal male suffrage, single-member arrondissement constituencies in two rounds for most of the period, with département lists in 1871, 1885, 1919, and 1924. classes.name: Élections aux assemblées constituantes et à l'Assemblée nationale (IVe République)
classes.name_en: Constituent Assembly and National Assembly elections (Fourth Republic)
classes.note: List proportional representation by département, with apparentements in 1951 and 1956; women voted from 1945. Seats count metropolitan France and overseas.

classes.name: Élections aux assemblées de la IIe République et au Corps législatif du Second Empire
classes.name_en: Second Republic assemblies and Second Empire Legislative Body elections
classes.note: The first elections by universal male suffrage: the Constituent Assembly (April 1848) and the Legislative Assembly (May 1849) by département lists, then the Corps législatif of the Second Empire (1852, 1857, 1863, and 1869) in single-member constituencies with official candidates. Dates to be enumerated from an official list.

classes.name: Élections à la Chambre des députés censitaire (Restauration et monarchie de Juillet)
classes.name_en: Chamber of Deputies elections under property suffrage (1815–1848)
classes.note: Elections by electoral colleges of taxpayers (about 90,000 electors under the Restoration, about 250,000 by 1846). No national series of results is known to us.

classes.name: Élections aux assemblées de la Révolution, du Consulat et de l'Empire
classes.name_en: Elections to the assemblies of the Revolution, the Consulate, and the Empire (1789–1815)
classes.note: The Estates-General (1789), the Legislative Assembly (1791), the Convention (1792), and the councils of the Directory (1795 to 1798) were chosen in two degrees by assemblies of electors; under the Consulate and Empire, lists of notables fed appointment by the Senate.
classes.disposition_reason: Two-degree elections in electoral assemblies, published as lists of the elected (Archives parlementaires) without a national series of vote counts.

classes.name: Élections au Sénat (IIIe République) et au Conseil de la République (IVe République)
classes.name_en: Senate (1876–1940) and Council of the Republic (1946–1958) elections
classes.note: The Third Republic Senate was elected in each département by a college of deputies, general and arrondissement councillors, and municipal delegates, renewed by thirds every three years (with 75 life senators until 1884); the Council of the Republic of the Fourth Republic was elected by similar colleges from 1946.

dates.quote: Deuxième République Louis-Napoléon Bonaparte 1848 - 1851

classes.name: Élection du président de la République de 1848
classes.note: The only direct presidential election before 1965: Louis-Napoléon Bonaparte, elected for four years under the Constitution of 4 November 1848.

classes.name: Élection du président de la République par le Parlement ou le collège électoral
classes.name_en: Presidential elections by Parliament or an electoral college (1871–1958)
classes.note: Third and Fourth Republic presidents were elected by the deputies and senators meeting as the Congress at Versailles (Thiers by the National Assembly in 1871); de Gaulle was elected on 21 December 1958 by a college of about 80,000 parliamentarians, councillors, and municipal delegates. The 1962 referendum introduced direct election.

classes.name: Plébiscites et référendums avant 1958
classes.note: Constitutional plebiscites of the Revolution and the Napoleonic era (1793, 1795, 1799 to 1800, 1802, 1804, and 1815), the Second Empire plebiscites of December 1851, November 1852, and May 1870, and the referendums of 21 October 1945 (two questions), 5 May 1946, and 13 October 1946.

classes.name_en: Paris, Lyon, and Marseille arrondissement and sector council elections
classes.note: Each sector elects a council (conseil d'arrondissement, or conseil de secteur in Marseille). Until 2020 one ballot per sector elected both the city councillors and the sector councillors, so those contests are municipal elections; from 2026 the sector councils have their own ballot (loi n° 2025-795). Paris has 17 sectors since 2020 (arrondissements 1 to 4 vote together as Paris Centre), Lyon 9, and Marseille 8.

classes.name: Élection des conseillers communautaires
classes.note: Since 2014, in communes of 1,000 inhabitants or more, the municipal ballot carries a second list of candidates for the commune's seats on its EPCI council (fléchage), and seats go to lists in proportion to the municipal result (Code électoral, art. L273-1 and following, loi n° 2013-403); smaller communes send members in the order of their municipal council. Before 2014 the municipal councils chose their delegates. No separate vote is cast, so the class holds the seat allocation rather than new vote counts.

classes.name: Élection des maires et des présidents des conseils départementaux, régionaux et communautaires
classes.name_en: Election of mayors and of the presidents of departmental, regional, and intercommunal councils by their councils
classes.note: Each council elects its executive (and deputies) by secret ballot at its first meeting, by absolute majority in two ballots and plurality in the third. Mayors have been elected by the council since 1882.
classes.disposition_reason: The ballots are minuted by each council and not collected; the Répertoire national des élus lists who holds each office, not the council votes.

classes.name: Référendums locaux et consultations locales
classes.note: Since 2003 a commune, département, region, or EPCI may submit a decision within its powers to a binding referendum (valid when half the registered voters take part), and may hold advisory consultations; communes held advisory consultations from 1992. The DGCL publishes no list.

classes.name: Consultations des électeurs d'une collectivité territoriale (art. 72-1, 72-4 et 73 de la Constitution)
classes.note: Votes on a collectivity's status or institutions, called by the President or by law: Corsica (6 July 2003), Guadeloupe, Martinique, Saint-Barthélemy, and Saint-Martin (7 December 2003), Mayotte (29 March 2009), Martinique and Guyane (10 and 24 January 2010), and Alsace (7 April 2013).

classes.name: Élection des commissions syndicales des sections de commune
classes.name_en: Elections of the boards of sections de commune
classes.note: The electors of a section de commune (a part of a commune holding its own property, such as common land) may elect a board when the prefect convenes them (CGCT, art. L2411-3).
classes.disposition_reason: Rare, convened case by case, and posted only locally; no collector.

classes.name: Élections des conseils d'arrondissement (1833–1940)
classes.note: Arrondissement councils were elected by canton alongside the general councils from 1833 (by property suffrage, then by universal male suffrage from 1848) until they were suspended in 1940 and not restored.
